 Zverev vs Fils Predictions, H2H History & Lines
 By 
 Juan Pablo Aravena
 in
 Tennis
 Published:
 November 19, 2026 at 8:24 am EST
 Tennis - U.S. Open - Flushing Meadows, New York, United States - September 13, 2026 Germany's Alexander Zverev in action during his men's singles final against Ben Shelton of the U.S. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Robert Deutsch 
 Zverev’s stronger Elo and 52-week serve-return profile make him the player to back
 The recent head-to-head and form point toward a Zverev win without a long match
 Zverev -2.5 games and Under 23.5 games are my Zverev vs Fils picks for this contest
 World No. 1 Alexander Zverev prepares to clash with No. 7 Arthur Fils in a pivotal group-stage match at the ATP World Tour Finals on November 19 at 2:30 PM ET.
 Zverev leads their career head-to-head 5-2, including a straight-sets win over Fils at Indian Wells in March 2026. Fils has the athleticism and shot-making to make this competitive, but the matchup history and the gap in their current underlying numbers favor the German.
 Zverev vs Fils Picks & Predictions
 The numbers point to Zverev as the more dependable player, with the total leaning under if he carries that advantage into the match. 
 Spread Pick: Zverev -2.5 Games (-108, Kalshi) – Claim the KALSHI PROMO CODE today 
 Tennis Abstract’s current Elo rates Zverev at 2,089.6 and Fils at 1,992.9, while Tennis Ratio’s 52-week comparison gives Zverev the edge in service games won (90.5% to 86.0%), first-serve accuracy (71.9% to 63.7%), and dominance ratio (2.098 to 1.318). Fils has shown he can compete, but these indicators favor Zverev controlling more of the key service and return exchanges.
 Zverev has won both of his opening matches in Turin in straight sets, while Fils split his first two matches, including a three-set win over Jodar and a three-set loss to Shelton. Their latest meeting was more one-sided: Zverev beat Fils 6-2, 6-3 at Indian Wells. That combination of recent form and matchup evidence supports backing Zverev while being cautious about an over.
 Zverev -2.5 games is the preferred side at -108. His 5-2 head-to-head lead, stronger Elo rating, higher service-game win rate, and recent straight-sets wins in Turin provide a sound basis for expecting him to win by at least three games. Fils’s strong shot-making could keep a set close, so this is not a call for a guaranteed blowout; the case is that Zverev has more ways to create the decisive break.
 Total Games Pick: Under 23.5 (-108, Kalshi)
 The Under 23.5 games is the better total at -108. Zverev’s latest win over Fils finished in 17 games, and his current Turin form has been efficient in straight sets. Fils’s serve can extend games, but Zverev’s advantage in service consistency and overall dominance makes a shorter match more plausible than the three-set or tiebreak-heavy script required to make the Over attractive.
